newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Optus sees steady 2nd half pay TV loss.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Optus sees steady 2nd half pay TV loss.

text.p: Optus Communications Pty Ltd chief executive officer Ziggy Switkowski said on Tuesday that losses from its pay television arm, Optus Vision, in the six months to June 30, were about the same level as the first half of 1996/97.
"They are running at about the same level," Switkowski told reporters after giving a speech to the Securities Institute of Australia luncheon.

Optus Vision reported a loss of A$168.2 million in the six months to December 31, 1996. The losses were mainly associated with the A$3.0 billion cost of building its cable network, which also carries telephony services.
Last month, Optus Communications moved to 100 percent control of Optus Vision from its previous 46.5 percent stake.
Switkowski said the group had laid off another 100 Optus Vison staff today, making a total of 350 staff layoffs or about 12 percent of the pay TV operator's workforce since the merger.
Losses from Optus Vision are expected to drag the Optus group into the red for the 1996/97 financial year, despite the profitability of Optus Commuications.
Optus Communications reported a net profit of A$58.9 million in the 1996/97 first half ending December 31.
